fundamentals.method: Earnings at risk from the company-specific issues, filings first. (1) Read NVDA's 10-K for FY ended 2026-01-25 (acc. 0001045810-26-000021), 10-Q for quarter ended 2026-07-26 (acc. 0001045810-26-000075), the Q1 FY27, Q2/Q3 FY26 10-Qs and FY25 10-K (to trace the geographic-definition change and risk-language changes), the Q2 FY27 CFO commentary, and every 8-K since 2026-10-01. (2) Sorted November 2026 headlines (cached Google News/finviz plus 18 fresh Google News RSS searches; headlines only) by evidentiary status. (3) Converted revenue-loss scenarios to EPS: lost revenue x 75.0% reported gross margin, operating expenses fixed, 16.5% tax, 24,285M diluted shares, on Zacks consensus FY27 (rev $407.63B, EPS $9.28) and FY28 (rev $683.05B, EPS $15.73); priced at today's 20.6x trailing (GAAP TTM EPS $7.91) and 13.5x forward (implied NTM EPS $12.10) held constant. (4) Balance-sheet capacity for one-off fines/settlements/write-offs from the 2026-07-26 balance sheet. fundamentals.headline: At today's multiples, filing-based earnings-at-risk scenarios put NVDA at about $148 if all China-headquartered billed revenue is lost, about $134 if the largest direct customer is lost or the short seller's alleged 20% of compute sales disappears, about $129 if data-center revenue falls 20%, and about $103 if it falls 35%. A fine is not the driver: a penalty equal to all $56.6B of cash and debt securities is $2.34/share (1.4% of the price), while the company-specific leg alone erased $574B, equivalent to a permanent loss of about 11% of revenue.

levels.label: Press-reported diverted volume ($7.5B, The Information) treated as one full year of lost revenue
levels.assumes: The reported $7.5B (described in headlines as accumulated over a multi-year relationship) is all lost in one year and never replaced; multiples unchanged.
levels.breaks_if: The diverted volume is larger than reported, or enforcement leads to licence conditions on other Southeast Asian intermediaries (the short seller names six more firms - allegation).
levels.sources: The Information 2026-11-10 and Fortune 2026-11-12 headlines via Google News RSS; 10-K FY26 and 10-Q Q2 FY27 income statements for TTM revenue.

levels.label: (a) Loss of all revenue from customers headquartered in China incl. Hong Kong
levels.assumes: Every dollar billed to China-HQ direct customers disappears and is not resold elsewhere; gross margin 75%, opex fixed; multiples stay 13.5x/20.6x. Note the definition is customer headquarters, not ship-to; Q3 guidance already assumes no China data-center compute revenue.
levels.breaks_if: Curbs extend beyond China-HQ customers (for example to Chinese-owned buyers in third countries or cloud access, as the RASA bill cited in the 10-Q would), or lost China volume forces inventory/purchase-obligation charges like the $4.5B H20 charge.

levels.label: (b) ALLEGATION: loss of the 'over 20%' of compute sales the short seller says reaches China via intermediaries
levels.basis: 20% x data-center compute share. Compute = 162,361 / 193,737 = 83.8% of FY26 data-center revenue (10-K; FY27 filings no longer split compute/networking); data center = 164,269 / 177,837 = 92.4% of H1 FY27 revenue. 0.20 x 0.838 x 0.924 = 15.5% of total revenue. FY27 EPS 9.28 -> 7.65 (-17.5%); FY28 15.73 -> 13.00 (-17.3%). Forward: 162.85 x (1 - 0.155 x 1.127) = 134.4. Trailing: 138.0. If 20% is applied to all data-center revenue (18.5% of total): 128.9 / 133.1.
levels.assumes: The short seller's figure is correct and all of that revenue is lost with no resale. This is an unverified allegation known here only from a headline (TIKR.com 2026-11-11 quoting 'over 20%' of compute sales; Culper Research, short since May 2026). Company filings state the opposite: over 99% of controlled data-center compute billed to Singapore was for US-based customers (Q2 FY26 10-Q) and H200 shipments to China were under 1% of data-center revenue (Q2 FY27 10-Q).
levels.breaks_if: Worse if the true share is higher (secondary outlets float 20-40%) or if a finding of diversion also brings penalties and licence denials for legitimate customers; better if investigators find the diverted volume is closer to the press-reported $7.5B (2.5% of TTM revenue).
levels.sources: TIKR.com 2026-11-11, MarketWatch 2026-11-10, Business Insider 2026-05-14 headlines (Google News RSS); 10-K FY26 Note 16; 10-Q Q2 FY27 Note 13; 10-Q Q2 FY26 (0001045810-25-000209) geographic footnote.

levels.label: (c) Loss of the largest single direct customer (16% of revenue)
levels.assumes: The customer's purchases vanish rather than re-route. Direct customers include ODMs, system integrators and distributors, so this overstates end-demand loss; the company also says it is supply-constrained, so freed supply could be resold.
levels.breaks_if: The lost customer is an end buyer whose demand is not replaced, or several top customers cut together (three direct customers were 16%, 15% and 13% of H1 FY27 revenue; five were 70% of receivables).
levels.sources: 10-Q 0001045810-26-000075 Note 13 (p.23), Note 7 (p.14), MD&A Concentration of Revenue (p.29).

levels.label: (d) Data-center revenue falls 20%
levels.assumes: A 20% cut versus the consensus path (FY28 consensus revenue $683B is +68% y/y), gross margin held at 75%, opex fixed, multiples unchanged.
levels.breaks_if: Gross margin falls with volume (Q3 guide is already 74.0%), or the $279B of supply and capacity commitments produce excess-inventory charges.
levels.sources: 10-Q 0001045810-26-000075 Note 13 market-platform table (p.24), Note 10 commitments (p.18); Zacks consensus.

levels.label: (c, severe) Loss of a direct customer the size of FY26's largest (22% of revenue)
levels.basis: FY26 largest direct customer = 22% of revenue (10-K Note 16). FY27 EPS 9.28 -> 6.97 (-24.9%); FY28 15.73 -> 11.85 (-24.6%). Forward: 162.85 x (1 - 0.22 x 1.127) = 122.5. Trailing: 127.5. For reference, stacking (a) 8.2% + (c) 16% = 24.2% of revenue gives 118.4 forward / 124.0 trailing.
levels.assumes: Concentration reverts to the FY26 level and that customer is lost entirely with no re-routing.
levels.breaks_if: Same as (c); also worse if receivables from that customer (largest AR balance is 22% of $63.1B) become doubtful.
levels.sources: 10-K 0001045810-26-000021 Note 16 and MD&A Concentration of Revenue; 10-Q Q2 FY27 Note 7.

levels.label: (d, severe) Data-center revenue falls 35% - lowest floor this method produces at constant multiples
levels.assumes: A 35% cut to data-center revenue versus consensus with the cost structure unchanged (opex fixed at about 9.5% of TTM revenue, so operating leverage stays near 1.13x); multiples do not compress further.
levels.breaks_if: Multiples compress as well (outside this method), gross margin drops, supply commitments ($279B) and guarantees ($108.5B gross maximum) crystallise, or equity-investment marks ($99B of investments) reverse through GAAP EPS.
levels.sources: 10-Q 0001045810-26-000075 Notes 6, 10, 13; Zacks consensus; StockAnalysis statistics for multiples.

Forward price = 162.85 x (1 - share x 1.127).

Already-priced test: the company-specific leg (186.64 -> 162.85, -12.7%) equals a permanent revenue loss of about 11.3% at constant forward multiple. The last column shows where each scenario lands if the 11-06 multiple was fair: (a) is already below-market at 169, (b)/(c) sit 5-6% under today's price, DC -35% is 118.

No other 8-K since 2026-10-01 (EDGAR list refreshed 2026-11-15T03:03Z): no Item 8.01/7.01 on inquiries, no 4.02, no 2.06. Earlier 8-Ks read: 2026-09-03 (Hugging Face, $11.9B + $1.0B retention, close H1 2027); 2026-08-17 (SB Energy guarantees capped at $105B, $1.5B investment).
Risk-language timeline in filings: 'regulatory and government inquiries and investigations' first appears in the Q3 FY26 10-Q; 'We have provided and will continue to provide assistance to authorities regarding attempted diversion' and 'any compliance failure at a customer or partner' first appear in the Q1 FY27 10-Q (2026-05-20); 'inquiries and investigations from foreign governments regarding sales of our products' first appears in the Q2 FY27 10-Q (2026-08-26). The 10-Q also states that a violation of export law 'even if the violation occurred without our knowledge' may bring penalties.

### 5. Balance-sheet capacity for a one-off fine, settlement or write-off (2026-07-26 balance sheet; 24,147M shares)
| Size | Per share | % of price / market cap | % of cash + debt securities ($56.6B) | % of TTM FCF ($127.0B) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| $10B cash penalty | $0.41 | 0.25% | 17.7% | 7.9% (29 days) |
| $25B | $1.04 | 0.64% | 44.2% | 19.7% (72 days) |
| $56.6B (all cash + debt securities) | $2.34 | 1.44% | 100% | 44.6% (163 days) |
| $127.0B (one year of FCF) | $5.26 | 3.23% | 224% | 100% |
| $10B pre-tax write-off (16.5% tax shield) | $0.35 | 0.21% | non-cash | non-cash |
Net cash (cash + debt securities less $33.4B notes) is $23.2B; marketable equity $42.8B is mostly locked up ($36.9B). Write-off candidates on the books: inventory $31.6B, non-marketable securities $51.2B, total equity investments $99B (full write-off about $3.42/share after tax, 43% of $229.0B equity). The $574B lost in the company-specific leg is 10.2x cash + debt securities and 4.5 years of TTM FCF, so the market is discounting earnings power and governance, not a payable fine.

### 6. What the 2026-11-17 report (and the 10-Q that normally follows the same day) can move
| Disclosure | Reference point | Effect on the numbers above |
|---|---|---|
| Q3 revenue and margin | Guide $108.0B +/-2% ($105.8-110.2B), GM 74.0%; consensus $108.9B, EPS $2.49 | Each 1% of permanent revenue = about 1.13% of EPS = about $1.84/share at today's multiple |
| Q4 outlook | Consensus $123.1B revenue, EPS $2.74 | A guide 10% below consensus maps to about -11% EPS (about $144) |
| China wording | 'Not assuming any Data Center compute revenue from China' | If kept, scenario (a) is limited to the non-compute China-HQ revenue; removal or new licence conditions enlarges it |
| Geographic and concentration tables | China-HQ 8.2%, Taiwan 28.0%, top customer 16% | Resets the shares used in (a) and (c) |
| Legal note and risk factors | No accrual; inquiries 'not material'; no mention of the new suits | First company confirmation of subpoenas, DOJ/BIS/SEC inquiries, new class actions, or a loss accrual |
| Charges | Q2 provisions $985M; H20 precedent $4.5B | Inventory/purchase-obligation charges, investigation costs, equity-investment marks (H1 gains $23.7B can reverse through GAAP EPS) |
| Capital return | $99.3B authorisation; Q2 buyback $19.7B | A paused buyback removes a bid worth about 2.5% of shares; continuation at these prices adds to EPS |
| Controls and timing | Interim CEO and CFO are the same person | A late 10-Q, a control deficiency or qualified certifications would be new information |
caveats: Multiples are held at today's 20.6x trailing and 13.5x forward by construction. Consensus EPS has barely moved (Zacks FY28 $15.61 -> $15.73 over 7 days; FY27 $9.62 -> $9.28) while the price fell, so today's multiple already embeds some earnings risk: applying an EPS cut to today's price may double-count, and further multiple compression (another analyst's method) would add to these declines.

The EPS conversion treats cost of revenue as fully variable and operating expenses as fixed. It ignores charges that a sudden demand loss would trigger (inventory $31.6B, supply commitments $279B; the H20 charge was $4.5B) and ignores mitigation: the 10-Q says the company is supply-constrained, so freed supply could be resold.

Scenario (b) rests on a short seller's allegation known here only from a secondary headline ('over 20%' of compute sales, TIKR.com 2026-11-11); the base, period and method of that claim could not be read. Company filings contradict it. The FY26 compute/networking mix was used because FY27 filings no longer split it.
China revenue in filings is defined by the direct customer's headquarters, not where chips are shipped or used. It is neither a measure of exports to China nor of diversion.

Direct customers include ODMs, system integrators and distributors; losing the 16% direct customer does not mean losing 16% of end demand, so (c) is likely overstated. Indirect customers above 10% exist but are not quantified in the 10-Q.

The 20.6x trailing multiple is on GAAP EPS of $7.91, which includes about $1.05/share of after-tax gains on equity securities. Excluding them the trailing P/E is about 23.7x, so the 'lowest in five years' reading is flattered, and those gains can reverse.
FY27 figures are pro forma run-rate sensitivities: three of four FY27 quarters are complete (FY27 ends January 2027). NTM leverage of 1.127x is interpolated between FY27 and FY28.

Balance-sheet figures are as of 2026-07-26. Since then: $1.5B SB Energy investment, pending $11.9B Hugging Face purchase, continued buybacks and dividends, and Q3 cash flow; none is visible until 2026-11-17. No size of fine or settlement is estimated.

News items are headlines from Google News RSS and finviz, not article text, and are unverified. Press reports of FBI, DOJ and Commerce activity are not confirmed by any company filing; allegations against individuals are not established (Reuters headline 2026-11-12: DOJ has not concluded the individual was a spy).

The only company filing on the events is the 2026-11-12 8-K. The board investigation and retention of outside counsel come from company newsroom statements and press coverage, not from an SEC filing, and the 8-K gives no reason for the resignation.
Page references are read from page footers in the EDGAR HTML text and may be off by one page.

The Culper Research report itself and the exact share of sales it alleges reaches China, with its definition and period

analogs.method: Historical analogs (event studies on real daily closes): NVDA's own 25%+ drawdowns and export-control shocks, plus 32 validated leadership-scandal / regulatory / export-action episodes at other large companies, measured from the pre-event close and from the day-5 close
analogs.headline: Analogs put the typical next-three-month closing low only about 7-9% below $162.85 (roughly $148-152, a zone the $148.80 intraday low on 11-12 already touched) with a bad-quartile outcome near $131-134; over twelve months the median analog made a lower low 20-25% below its day-5 close ($122-130), with the bad quartile near $98-110. NVDA's own deep drawdowns (2018, 2021-22) map to $105 and $80; the day-5 close held within 5% of the eventual low in 41% of analogs over 60 sessions but only 19% over 250.

levels.label: Mild quartile: 60-session closing low if NVDA follows the better 25% of analogs
levels.basis: 75th percentile of the further fall from day-5 close to the lowest close in sessions 6-60 = -4.0% (all 32 analogs; also -4.0% for the 20 severity-matched ones). 162.85 x (1 - 0.040) = 156.34. Day-5 close was within 5% of the 60-session low in 41% of analogs (45% severity-matched, 44% of the 9 leadership+regulatory cases).
levels.assumes: The 2026-11-17 report and guidance hold, and no new enforcement step (charges, subpoena, enacted export law) arrives in the next three months.
levels.breaks_if: A close below about $154.7 (5% under the day-5 close): history then shifts to the median or bad-quartile path. Over 250 sessions the day-5 close held within 5% in only 19% of analogs.
levels.sources: stockanalysis.com daily close series (32 analog tickers, SPY, QQQ); NVDA pickle

levels.label: NVDA's own export-control template
levels.basis: Four validated NVDA export shocks (t0 2022-09-01, 2022-10-07, 2023-10-17, 2025-04-16): further fall from day-5 close to the 60-session low = -19.7%, -6.1%, -6.2%, 0.0%; median -6.15% -> 162.85 x 0.9385 = 152.83. Adding 5 other chip export events (AMAT 2023, LRCX 2022, SNPS 2025, MU 2018, SWKS 2019; n=9): median -6.1% ($152.92), bad quartile -7.5% ($150.64), worst -25.1% ($121.97).
levels.assumes: The China/export overhang behaves like the 2022-2025 curbs, where lost China revenue was absorbed and the pre-event close was regained in 12-50 sessions.
levels.breaks_if: The diversion probe produces charges or penalties, or legislation reaches a broader product set; none of these nine events included a leadership exit or a criminal inquiry into the company itself except AMAT 2023 (-3.8%).

levels.label: Median analog 60-session closing low
levels.basis: Median further fall day-5 -> 60-session low = -8.4% (n=32) -> $149.17. Subsets: leadership -9.3% ($147.70), regulatory -7.5% ($150.64), severity-matched (day-5 loss >=10%) -6.8% ($151.78), leadership+regulatory -7.9% ($149.98). Pre-event route: median low within 60 sessions -20.8% x 186.64 = $147.91. NVDA cross-checks: since-2016 median drawdown depth -37.6% x 239.24 = $149.29; 2025 depth -36.9% = $150.96; intraday low 11-12 = $148.80.
levels.assumes: This is an ordinary leadership/regulatory shock. Note the same 32 stocks fell a median 7.9% over sessions 6-60 from any random day, so this level is roughly normal volatility, not an event premium.
levels.breaks_if: A decisive close below $147-149 (the cluster above plus the 11-12 intraday low): 25% of analogs went on to lose 19% or more.

levels.label: Lowest NVDA trough multiple applied to today's earnings
levels.basis: Lowest trailing P/E at any NVDA drawdown trough with SEC TTM coverage: 2018-12-24 close 3.177 / TTM diluted EPS 0.18725 (10-Q filed 2018-11-15) = 16.97x. 16.97 x 7.91 (TTM EPS, quarter ended 2026-07-26) = $134.21. Other trough P/Es: 43.5x (2020), 36.8x (2022), 57.8x (2024), 32.0x (2025); today 20.6x.
levels.assumes: The market prices NVDA at its most depressed historical trough multiple while TTM earnings stay at $7.91.
levels.breaks_if: Earnings fall. The 17.0x trough in 2018 was followed by a 48% drop in TTM EPS (0.18725 -> 0.09775 by the Oct-2019 quarter); a repeat would make this multiple meaningless as a floor.
levels.sources: SEC EDGAR companyfacts CIK0001045810 (TTM EPS); NVDA daily closes

levels.label: Bad-quartile analog 60-session closing low
levels.basis: 25th percentile of further fall day-5 -> 60-session low = -19.3% (n=32) -> $131.38. Subsets: leadership -17.4% ($134.47), regulatory -17.9% ($133.70), severity-matched -17.5% ($134.31). Worst NVDA export-shock path -19.7% = $130.77 (Sept-Oct 2022).
levels.assumes: A second leg of bad news inside three months, as in UNH 2025 (-24.7%), JD 2018 (-27.4%), PZZA 2018 (-24.4%), BABA 2020 (-23.6%), BA 2024 (-17.4%).
levels.breaks_if: The episode turns into an accounting/auditor problem: SMCI 2024 (-59.2%) and Valeant 2015 (-61.4%) are the two 60-session outcomes beyond this band.

levels.label: Median analog 12-month (250-session) closing low
levels.basis: Median further fall day-5 -> 250-session low = -24.7% (n=32) -> $122.63. Subsets: leadership -26.4% ($119.94), regulatory -22.2% ($126.70), severity-matched -20.0% ($130.20), leadership+regulatory -24.7% ($122.63). Market-relative version -26.1%. Pre-event route: median low within 250 sessions -36.3% x 186.64 = $118.89. Baseline for the same stocks from a random day: -16.9%, so about 8 points is event-specific (21 of 32 events were worse than their own stock's median).
levels.assumes: The overhang lingers for a year and the stock makes a later, lower low (the 250-session low came at a median of session 108; only 41% were in by session 60).
levels.breaks_if: Fast resolution: 14 of 32 analogs regained the pre-event close within 60 sessions and 22 within 250. Conversely, 10 of the 32 lows coincided with market-wide lows (Dec 2018, Mar 2020, Apr 2025, 2000), so a broad bear market pushes below this.

levels.label: NVDA 2018 repeat (scandal plus earnings downcycle)
levels.basis: 2018 closing drawdown -56.1% (7.234 on 2018-10-01 -> 3.177 on 2018-12-24) applied to the 239.24 peak: 239.24 x 0.439 = $105.03. Related: 10 of NVDA's 13 completed 25%+ drawdowns since 1999 went beyond today's -31.9%, and from that level fell a further median 33.9% ($107.64; quartiles -13.7% / -52.2%). Severity-matched analog bad quartile at 250 sessions -32.6% = $109.76; leadership bad quartile -36.8% = $103.00.
levels.assumes: A genuine earnings decline arrives on top of the scandal, as in 2018 when TTM EPS fell 48% in the following year.
levels.breaks_if: Holds as a floor only if earnings fall no more than roughly a third: at $105 the trailing P/E on $7.91 would be 13.3x, below any NVDA trough multiple in the SEC-covered record.
levels.sources: stockanalysis.com NVDA daily closes since 1999; SEC EDGAR companyfacts

levels.label: Bad-quartile analog 12-month closing low
levels.basis: 25th percentile of further fall day-5 -> 250-session low = -39.6% (n=32) -> $98.32. Regulatory subset -46.0% ($87.94); pre-event route bad quartile -47.9% x 186.64 = $97.29. Cases at or beyond this: WYNN 2018 -46.0%, MU 2018 -47.9%, BBY 2012 -48.3%, BABA 2020 -51.9%, MSFT 2000 -53.4%, UAA 2019 -56.1%, SMCI 2024 -59.2%, Valeant -89.7%.
levels.assumes: The scandal coincides with a business or market downturn; most of these cases overlapped one (China crackdown, dot-com bust, Dec 2018, COVID).
levels.breaks_if: Fraud, restatement or loss of the franchise; then the tail cases below apply.

levels.label: NVDA 2021-22 repeat (full bear-market drawdown)
levels.basis: 2021-22 closing drawdown -66.4% (33.376 on 2021-11-29 -> 11.227 on 2022-10-14) applied to 239.24 = $80.38. NVDA's bottom-quartile depth across all 13 completed episodes since 1999 is also -66.4%.
levels.assumes: A 2022-style combination of collapsing demand, inventory correction and a market-wide derating (QQQ fell alongside).
levels.breaks_if: Only deeper precedents are NVDA 2000 (-67.8%), 2008 (-85.1%) and 2002 (-89.7%), all when it was a small cyclical graphics supplier.

levels.label: Worst analog excluding the levered case (accounting scandal path)
levels.basis: SMCI 2024: day-5 close to lowest close within 60 and 250 sessions = -59.2% (short report, 10-K delay, auditor resignation). 162.85 x 0.408 = $66.44. Worst leadership-subset outcome: UAA 2019 -56.1% ($71.49), which overlapped COVID.
levels.assumes: The board investigation finds the financial statements cannot be relied on.
levels.breaks_if: Nothing in the facts supplied indicates an accounting issue; this is a tail marker, not a forecast.

levels.label: Worst analog in the set (Valeant) - not a credible floor for NVDA
levels.basis: BHC (Valeant) t0 2015-09-28: day-5 close to lowest close within 250 sessions = -89.7% -> $16.77. NVDA's own worst drawdown (-89.7%, 2002) applied to 239.24 = $24.64.
levels.assumes: Fraud allegations plus a debt-funded business model that stops working; Valeant carried heavy debt, NVDA holds more cash than debt and $127.0B of trailing free cash flow.
levels.breaks_if: Reported for completeness because the worst case was requested; it requires both fraud and balance-sheet stress.

caveats: Event dates, descriptions and tags (who left, what the regulator did) come from memory; only the price reaction on or next to each date was checked against downloaded prices. No news text was read to confirm what caused each move.

Small sample: 32 episodes, 16 in the leadership subset, 9 with both leadership and regulatory elements, 5 chip export actions. Quartiles on these counts move several points if one or two cases are added or removed.

No analog combines a founder-CEO exit, a criminal diversion inquiry and export legislation at a $3.9T company. The closest partial matches (UNH 2025, WYNN 2018, AIG 2005, Marsh 2004, UAA 2019) are different businesses with different earnings sensitivity.

Selection bias runs both ways. Requiring a visible reaction drops muted cases (AAPL 2011, TXN 2018, INTC 2018) and slow-burn ones (WFC 2016, LULU 2013); only tickers the provider still serves were used, so bankrupt or delisted scandal names (for example Enron, WorldCom, Tyco, Nikola) are absent and the tail is understated.

At 60 sessions the analog median (-8.4%) is almost the same as what those stocks do from a random day (-7.9%), so the $148-152 zone reflects ordinary volatility more than a scandal effect. The event effect shows mainly in the tail and at 250 sessions.

250-session windows pick up unrelated shocks: 10 of 32 lows fell on market-wide lows, and some cases had later company problems (TSLA 2019 demand, BBY 2012 earnings). Benchmark-relative figures did not soften the medians, but high-beta stocks fall more than the benchmark in crashes.
Events are not independent: four share the December 2018 low, three share COVID, LRCX 2022 is the same shock as NVDA's own October 2022 event, and the first two NVDA export shocks share one trough.

Valuation differs from every NVDA precedent: past troughs came at 17-58x trailing earnings, today is 20.6x. Applying past percentage depths may overstate downside if earnings hold, and understate it if the 11-17 report or the investigation changes the earnings base.

Earnings on 2026-11-17 fall on session 7 of the episode. Few analogs had a scheduled report that early (UAA, KHC and AMAT reported at t0), so the next week is less comparable than the averages suggest.

Analog data are closes only, so intraday undercuts are not captured; NVDA's own troughs were undercut intraday by 2-8%. Returns exclude dividends. Pre-2009 NVDA closes are small split-adjusted numbers rounded to four decimals, so the 1999 depths carry about half a point of rounding error.
AIG 2005 (-3.02% on t0, z -1.9) and MU 2018 (-5.5%, z -1.7) pass the validation rule only on the raw-move leg; AMAT 2023, UAA 2019 and KHC 2019 coincided with earnings releases.
The Valeant and SMCI tails involved accounting or leverage problems that nothing in the supplied facts indicates for NVDA; they are reported because the worst case was requested, not as likely paths.
unavailable: Intraday highs and lows for the analog tickers and for NVDA before 2016-11-21 (the long series is close-only)

News text or filings to confirm the cause and exact timing of each analog event (headlines only are reachable; none were used)
Price histories for delisted or foreign-listed scandal cases (for example Tyco, Enron, WorldCom, Nikola, Luckin, Volkswagen, Nissan), which would have filled out the tail
Point-in-time valuation and estimate data for the analog companies at their event dates, needed to match cases on starting multiple
